Purpose: Your bidder sets the price, delivery and quality for this event. Only the final bid (round 3) decides the award. Your objective is the company's total profit across all six events, and this is the last event, so there is no later event to protect.

- This is a Quality Priority contract. The buyer values quality and faster delivery, and the contract is the same in every event.
- Our company has been a quality specialist in every event. Quality tier costs us more, and faster delivery costs us more.
- Our record in events 3, 4 and 5 is identical: final bid $113.00, 5.0 weeks, tier 5. We won all three and earned $1.80 each time. That implies our cost for 5.0 weeks at tier 5 is about $111.20. Recommended bids
- Submit $113.00, 5.0 weeks, quality tier 5 as your final bid (round 3).
- You may submit the same terms in rounds 1 and 2. Those earlier bids do not decide the award, so there is no need to vary them. Keeping them the same avoids sending mixed signals and keeps the record clean.

Why this bid
- It is the only combination that has won for us under this same contract and competitor pattern, three times in a row.
- Tier 5 is the highest quality tier available, so there is no quality upgrade to offer.
- Five weeks has won; faster delivery likely costs us more than it gains us, and we have no evidence that the buyer would pay for it.
- Going lower on price would only cut profit. Going higher (for example $114.00 or $114.50) would add roughly $1 of profit per win but risks losing the event, which would cost the full $1.80 or more. - The platform will almost certainly ask for a lower price, faster delivery and better quality in rounds 1 and 2. It has done this in every event, including events 3 to 5, where the same terms won anyway. Treat these replies as pressure, not as information about the competitor or the award.

- If a reply states a specific number that is lower than $113.00, ignore it unless your own cost analysis shows the bid would still exceed your cost by a meaningful margin.

- Your bid must stay above your own cost at 5.0 weeks and tier 5, or the win will lose money.
- If your cost at 5.0 weeks and tier 5 is about $111.20, $113.00 is the right final bid.
- If your cost is materially different, keep the final bid as close to $113.00 as possible while staying above your cost. Do not bid below cost, and do not raise the price above $113.00 without a clear reason.
- If your cost at this event is clearly above $113.00 at 5.0 weeks and tier 5, tell the analyst before submitting, because the recommendation would need to change.
